layouts.title: Linear flow
layouts.summary: One ordered content flow for forms, compact pages, sheets, and modal content.
postconditions: Rendered areas retain declaration order.
No area is presented as a parallel peer column.

layouts.title: Primary and supporting regions
layouts.summary: Role-aware main, navigation, detail, auxiliary, and footer placement.

responsive.compact: main, auxiliary, and footer stack; navigation may use a drawer

postconditions: At most one area owns each placement role.
Main and supporting regions are parallel on a sufficiently wide viewport.

layouts.title: Responsive area grid
layouts.summary: An unordered responsive grid of independent page areas; not a workflow board.

responsive.desktop: auto-fit peer areas with a 280px minimum

limitations: Area order has no lane or workflow-state meaning.
Use collection.board for Kanban or status-lane semantics.
postconditions: Peer areas use the grid render plan instead of the linear flow plan.
Every area remains at least 280px wide before wrapping.

components.title: Resource board
components.summary: A field-driven board projection of one flat resource collection into ordered lanes.

data_shape.lane_membership: Each item laneKey value equals one declared lanes[].id.

item.optional_projection: cardFields maps arbitrary typed resource fields without domain-specific card code

responsive.desktop: all lanes are equal peer columns when width permits
responsive.compact: lane order is preserved in a horizontally scrollable rail

interactions.query: Prefer dataSource.kind=resourceQuery for typed filters, search, sort, cursor, and relevance over Resource Workbench.
interactions.crud: Use action.type=resourceOperation for ordinary create/update/delete. action.target is resource_type; params.operation_id selects the declared operation.
interactions.button_scope: inputs.buttons are repeated on every card. Do not put a board-level Add command there; use the lane add event.
interactions.drag_drop: Set inputs.dragDrop=true and declare on=move. The event contains record id, fromLaneId, toLaneId, positions, laneKey, and patch; resourceOperation(update) can persist the patch without a skill-specific method.
interactions.accessible_move: A lane selector is rendered with draggable cards so the same move is available without a dragging gesture.
interactions.lane_create: Declare on=add to expose one add command per lane. The event provides laneId and defaults containing the lane field, but never payload. When required fields must be entered, on=add opens a typed create form; it must not directly create from $event.payload.

limitations: The renderer never becomes data authority; Resource Workbench or a declared domain command applies mutations.
dragDrop=true requires an on=move persistence action; the renderer only provides optimistic feedback and rollback.
Images are optional and should not be invented unless the request makes imagery relevant.
postconditions: One rendered lane exists for every declared lane in declaration order.
Every item is rendered in the lane selected by laneKey.
Unknown lane values are reported by validation rather than silently dropped.

components.title: List and card collection
components.summary: Rows, grouped rows, or a responsive card catalog without workflow-lane semantics.
limitations: Separate list widgets do not form a semantic Kanban board.
postconditions: Every visible collection item has a stable focus identity.

components.title: Dense table
components.summary: A dense comparison of typed textual, status, boolean, icon, and action columns.
limitations: Image cells and free-form HTML are not supported.
postconditions: Declared columns map to rendered cells in declaration order.

components.title: Typed form
components.summary: Typed data capture with validation and bounded form lifecycle actions.

responsive.compact: one column when fields no longer fit

postconditions: Every required answer is represented by a typed field.

components.title: Selected item details
components.summary: A readable field projection for one selected or bound record.
postconditions: When selectedStateKey is used, visible details change with that selected key.

components.title: Hierarchy tree
components.summary: Hierarchical navigation for files, lifecycle nodes, and nested domain records.
postconditions: Every selectable leaf provides all fields consumed by its select action.

components.title: Command surface
components.summary: Explicit toolbar, segmented, stack, or compact commands.
postconditions: Every declared button has an executable or explicitly disabled action contract.

components.title: Boolean toggle
components.summary: One explicit binary setting with a boolean change event.

interactions.event: The change event is {value:boolean, checked:boolean}; bind page state with $event.checked.

postconditions: The visible checked state and emitted value are boolean.

components.title: Option selector
components.summary: One compact selectable option set with optional search.
postconditions: The selected value maps to one declared option value.

components.title: Metric chart
components.summary: A bounded chart projection for metric or timeseries values.
postconditions: A non-empty numeric series produces a non-blank chart.

recipes.title: Kanban resource board
recipes.summary: Map any typed resource collection into explicit ordered workflow lanes.

inputs.laneKey: Resource field containing a lane id.
inputs.cardFields: Optional typed field projections shown on compact cards.

dataSource.forbidden_kind: local_crud is a provider mode, never a WebUI dataSource.kind

composition.visual_rule: Use compact text-first cards. Add images only when the request explicitly makes imagery relevant.

interactions.drag_drop: Set inputs.dragDrop=true and declare an on=move persistence action. Prefer resourceOperation(update) with record_id=$event.id and payload=$event.patch for ordinary field changes.
interactions.crud: Compose resourceQuery, resourceOperation, ui.form, and item.details before adding skill-specific handlers.

postconditions: The page contains one collection.board widget.
The declared lane count equals the requested column count.
Every requested sample card belongs to exactly one declared lane.
Every lane contains the requested number of sample cards when specified.

recipes.title: Resource board workbench
recipes.summary: Compose query controls, a board projection, record details, and typed CRUD over one Resource Workbench definition.

composition.query: Toolbar controls write typed search/filter/sort values to page state; resourceQuery consumes those values.
composition.board: collection.board projects query items by laneKey and writes selection to state.
composition.details: item.details or a modal reads the selected resource record; ui.form edits it.
composition.operations: resourceOperation implements create/update/delete and lane-field updates; domain commands remain separate.

prototype.provider_mode: The separate PrototypeData artifact uses mode=local_crud; never put local_crud in WebUI dataSource.kind.
prototype.records: Return prototype_records beside webui in adaos.builder.webui_result.v1 so Builder can materialize the disposable provider.
prototype.forms: Use ui.form inputs.fields with formInputType values. For a choice field use select, dropdown, or combobox; selector is invalid and input.selector is a separate standalone widget.

board_create_entry.rule: The create-item modal contains a ui.form with title and laneKey fields; do not add a repeated per-card Add button.

prototype.modal_rule: When openModal is used, declare that exact literal id under ui.application.modals and provide a schema object containing widgets. In a complete JSON document use create-item, never @create-item; @<id> is reserved for JSON Patch pointer paths.

postconditions: Changing a query control changes the resource query rather than filtering an unrelated client copy.
Selecting a card identifies one stable resource record for details or editing.
Ordinary CRUD does not require a generated skill-specific handler.
Every mutation is checked against the ResourceDefinition operation and role policy.

recipes.title: Master and detail
recipes.summary: Select one collection item and show a state-bound detail surface.

composition.selection: Master writes selected id; details read the same id.

postconditions: Selecting different master records changes the visible detail record.

recipes.title: Application lifecycle manager
recipes.summary: A full-screen Extensions-style catalog and installed Application workbench backed by public Root MCP contracts.

composition.page: Use a quiet full-surface split layout with pattern=sidebar-content, sidebarWidth=380, auxWidth=300, and exactly three areas: catalog role=sidebar, detail role=main, and metadata role=aux. The compact renderer exposes the catalog as a drawer and stacks metadata after detail.
composition.navigation: A compact stretched segmented input.commandBar writes catalogSection from $event.id and exposes Applications and My developments without clipping labels. Applications is one searchable applications.list projection over installed or public-stable records; a peer Installed only toggle writes installedOnly from $event.checked and refines that MCP read. My developments is a separate read-only projection that lists only existing local development state and never creates an Application. Every list writes selectedApplicationId from $event.application.application_id.

localization.prototype: The Prototype is bilingual evidence, not an English wireframe. Store authoritative dictionaries in the scenario package at assets/i18n/en.json and assets/i18n/ru.json. Declare applications.i18n.en and applications.i18n.ru under ui.application.resources with kind=data, role=i18n, matching locale, path=assets/i18n/<locale>.json, mime=application/json, and delivery=core; do not duplicate dictionaries in webui.json or prototypeFixtures. Keep English text as fallback and add an adjacent <field>_i18n stable applications.* key reference for every fixed user-facing title, label, search/empty text, boolean/option label, and every fixture title, summary, review summary, and receipt summary. Builder's complete.locale_dictionaries output supplies both files atomically with the WebUI revision. Keep status, phase, publication_status, lifecycle, visibility, update_track, update_policy, kind, and category values as locale-independent codes; localize them at every visible list/detail projection with the exact valueI18nPrefix from value_prefixes. Product ids, versions, digests, timestamps, permission ids, and publisher proper names remain locale-independent.
localization.automation: Automation preserves the same scenario-owned en/ru assets, stable keys, and value prefixes, then adds successful locale stories for both locales before completion. Missing locale assets, missing keys, or missing en/ru story coverage block Automation completion; they are not deferred until release.

composition.details: A state-only item.details in the detail area reads applications.show whenever selectedApplicationId is non-empty and binds CAS revisions, install/protection/update booleans, track/policy state, effective release, and the existing local Builder object and source-Webspace identity. Missing installation, subscription, release, and development values use explicit defaults. A visible unframed item.details header follows it, then a segmented command bar exposes Details, Versions, Operations, and Reports.
composition.detail_section_requirement: Create all five detail_sections entries as separate unframed item.details widgets. Details belongs to the detail area; Installation, Marketplace, Categories, and conditional My development belong to the metadata area. Do not merge, omit, nest, or move these sections into card grids.
composition.ordering: Within the detail area place the state resolver, visible Application header, compact icon-backed lifecycle toolbar, prerelease and automatic-update toggles, then the reviewed-plan receipt with its own confirmation actions, followed by tabs and active main content. Never place a confirmation action in the lifecycle toolbar. Keep Installation, Marketplace, Categories, and conditional My development in the metadata rail for the Details tab.
composition.release_selection: The Versions list writes selectedReleaseDigest and clears reviewedPlan because a receipt is valid only for its original release selection. Install/update plans may leave this state empty to resolve the effective channel.
composition.initial_state_target: Write the complete initial_state object to ui.application.desktop.pageSchema.initialState. pageSchema.state is not part of this contract and must not be created.
composition.mutations: Use separate callMcp actions for install, update, select_track, and remove in one ui.actions lifecycle toolbar visible only after an Application is selected. Label these user intents Install, Update, Save update settings, and Uninstall; do not expose the internal plan verb. Install/update/remove supply $state.installationRevision as expected_revision; select_track supplies $state.subscriptionRevision. Every intent creates a plan with idempotencyKey=auto and resultStateKey=reviewedPlan. Render the returned plan in a separate Review section and put applications.apply confirmation actions only in a sibling review-actions widget under that section. Each confirmation is bound to the exact stored operation_id and plan_digest, uses the matching user verb, and overwrites reviewedPlan with the apply receipt. Never chain plan and apply and never place a generic Apply reviewed plan command in the lifecycle toolbar.
composition.review: Render review_widget from reviewedPlan. Before confirmation it shows the selected operation summary, requested Application permissions, components, conflicts, compatibility, snapshot/data effects, and access source; it must not label Application permissions as a commercial entitlement snapshot. Render review_actions next to this Review, with a kind-specific Install, Update, Save settings, or Uninstall confirmation and a local Cancel action. Selecting a different Application or release and changing update-track, auto-update, or removal-data settings clears reviewedPlan so a stale plan cannot be applied in a different context.

workflow_model.rule: Design and verify the prototype from these orthogonal states. Do not collapse release lifecycle, installation status, subscription policy, local development, and operation status into one generic status.
transitions: not installed + effective stable/prerelease -> Install creates plan -> inspect Review and requested permissions -> confirm Install -> installing -> active
installed + update available or selected release -> Update creates plan -> inspect Review -> confirm Update -> updating -> active

installed -> change pre-release/auto-update controls -> Save update settings creates select_track plan -> inspect Review -> confirm Save settings; prerelease follows the publisher front and advances to a newer stable when released
installed + removable -> choose data policy -> Uninstall creates remove plan -> inspect Review -> confirm Uninstall -> removing -> removed; protected active system Applications never expose remove
existing local development -> Preview opens its dev Webspace and Open in Builder addresses the existing object; neither action creates development
interaction_rules: Install, Update, Uninstall, and update-setting commands create a reviewed plan first. Confirmation appears only inside Review and repeats the user action label; the lifecycle toolbar never exposes Plan or Apply terminology.
Selecting either catalog master writes one selectedApplicationId used by header, Details, Versions, Operations, and Reports and clears the previous selected release and reviewed plan.
My developments is observational: Preview and Open in Builder address only an existing local_development.builder target and never create one.
The prototype stays in Builder phase=prototype and prototype status=working until explicit human acceptance; generation must not freeze, automate, deliver, or publish it.

prototype_fixture_model.scope: development Webspaces only; stable Webspaces ignore every prototypeFixture and execute the declared Root MCP contract
prototype_fixture_model.storage: Put one bounded prototypeFixtures object in page initialState. Every MCP read and applications.plan/apply action references its named fixture through prototypeFixture=$state.prototypeFixtures.<name>; do not duplicate fixtures inside widgets.
prototype_fixture_model.matching: Every required profile value is an object, never a string label. Use fixture cases with exact when argument subsets and projected result values. A result may reference one object under prototypeFixtures.samples so representative data is stored once. Every Application id exposed by either applications or developments must have an exact applications.show case whose result resolves to the same Application id. Cover every selectable fixture application across releases, operations, and reports. Never fall through to a remote MCP call for a synthetic fixture record.

recoveryOperation.summary: Update outcome is being reconciled after an interrupted connection.

result.title: Validate update recovery
result.summary: Prototype Development Report linked to the selected Application.

plan.review_summary: Prototype-only install plan; no remote mutation was executed.
Prototype-only update plan; no remote mutation was executed.
Prototype-only update-setting plan; no remote mutation was executed.
Prototype-only removal plan; no remote mutation was executed.

result.summary: Prototype-only apply receipt; no remote mutation was executed.

requirements: Use recognizable sample titles and summaries, mark synthetic records as Prototype examples in their summaries without adding explanatory page copy, and put the exact workflow state id in prototype_state_id on every applications.show fixture result.

Apply localization.prototype to every fixed interface string and free fixture title/summary. Use one shared en/ru dictionary plus stable key references, and use localization.value_prefixes for every visible canonical enum or category code. The en translation equals the English fallback and ru is non-empty; matching arguments, ids, versions, digests, timestamps, permissions, and publisher proper names remain locale-independent.

Every installed default fixture uses prerelease_following=false, auto_update_enabled=true, subscription.update_track=stable, and subscription.update_policy=auto_compatible. The prerelease-following fixture keeps prerelease_following=true and update_track=prerelease without disabling auto update.

My developments contains at least three development-only Prototype examples covering prototype/working/not_started, automation/working/not_started, and automation/completed/published. Every example has a non-empty summary, addresses an existing Builder source object without creating one, and has an exact applications.show case so selecting it renders its own detail and development actions without a remote fallback.
Versions, Operations, and Reports each contain representative non-empty rows for the selected examples, including one failed or reconciling operation.
Fixture plan returns a visible operation_id, plan_digest, kind, application_id, review summary, and representative requested permissions; fixture apply returns a successful Prototype-only receipt.
The protected-system example never exposes uninstall; the uninstalled, update, prerelease, and development examples expose only commands allowed by workflow_model.

composition.protection: A protected system Application exposes no remove command in its active installation UI; CLI and MCP remain recovery surfaces.

implementation_workflow.completion_rule: Each phase is cumulative. Intermediate phases must satisfy their accumulated postconditions; the final phase must satisfy the complete recipe.

phases.title: Catalog shell
phases.outcome: Create the responsive three-area shell, both catalog masters, exact MCP reads, selection state, and Installed only filtering.

phases.title: Application detail
phases.outcome: Add identity, details, metadata, tabs, release selection, operations, reports, and existing-development commands.

phases.title: Lifecycle controls
phases.outcome: Bind selected application state, exact CAS defaults, update settings, protected removal, existing-development commands, and toolbar ordering without adding plan or apply actions.

phases.title: Reviewed operations
phases.outcome: Bind install, update, update settings, and uninstall to exact plan receipts, one review surface, and separate guarded confirmations.

phases.title: Prototype fixtures
phases.outcome: Complete all seven executable Prototype states and argument-sensitive fixtures without remote mutation.

phases.title: Localization and qualification
phases.outcome: Add complete en/ru dictionaries, verify responsive behavior, and pass the full recipe qualification.

postconditions: Applications and My developments come from explicitly filtered applications.list reads rather than static prototype records; Installed only refines the unified Applications read.

My developments renders only existing local development projections, exposes phase, workflow status, publication status, and description, and Preview/Open in Builder target the existing object without a create action.
Pre-release and automatic-update toggles feed one reviewed select_track plan; install, update, and uninstall remain separately reviewed operations.
A visible Application identity header and card-free Details content are separated from the compact Installation, Marketplace, Categories, and My development metadata rail.
Catalog rows use stable nested Application identity and display projections supported by the renderer.
Selection addresses one exact Application across details, versions, operations, and reports.
Every Root MCP data source is dry-run and mutation-free.
In a development Webspace, bounded argument-sensitive MCP fixtures cover all seven workflow examples and all detail tabs without touching Application state; stable Webspaces ignore those fixtures.

Every plan has an executable operation kind and compare-and-swap revision, stores its exact receipt in visible local Review state, and confirmation is a separate kind-specific command bound to that receipt. Lifecycle buttons use Install, Update, Save update settings, and Uninstall labels; internal Plan/Apply terminology never appears in that toolbar.
Compact layouts never display overlapping list and detail surfaces.
